source.text: בְּ֭נִי לְחָכְמָתִ֣י הַקְשִׁ֑יבָה לִ֝תְבוּנָתִ֗י הַט־אָזְנֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: My son, to my wisdom pay attention; to my understanding incline your ear,

en.L: My son, to my wisdom pay attention; \q to my understanding incline your ear,
en.B: My son, listen closely to the wisdom I have; \q bend your ear to what I understand,
en.R: My son, pay attention to my wise teaching. \q Listen carefully to what I understand.

fr.L: Mon fils, à ma sagesse sois attentif ; \q à mon intelligence incline ton oreille,
fr.B: Mon fils, écoute bien la sagesse que j’ai ; \q tends l’oreille à ce que je comprends,
fr.R: Mon fils, fais attention à mon enseignement plein de sagesse. \q Écoute bien ce que je comprends.

sw.L: Mwanangu, hekima yangu isikilize; \q kwa ufahamu wangu tega sikio lako,
sw.B: Mwanangu, isikilize kwa makini hekima niliyo nayo; \q elekeza sikio lako kwa yale ninayoyafahamu,
sw.R: Mwanangu, sikiliza kwa makini mafundisho yangu ya hekima. \q Sikiliza vizuri yale ninayoyaelewa.

decisions.choice: my wisdom ... my understanding: what the father has learned
decisions.reason: The father speaks of wisdom he has gained by living, as in 4:3–4.

source.text: לִשְׁמֹ֥ר מְזִמּ֑וֹת וְ֝דַ֗עַת שְׂפָתֶ֥יךָ יִנְצֹֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: to keep discretion, and knowledge your lips will guard.

en.L: to keep discretion, \q and your lips will guard knowledge.
en.B: so that you keep your foresight \q and your lips guard what you know.
en.R: Then you will make wise choices, \q and you will say what is true and wise.

fr.L: pour garder la réflexion, \q et tes lèvres garderont la connaissance.
fr.B: afin que tu conserves ta prévoyance \q et que tes lèvres veillent sur ce que tu sais.
fr.R: Alors tu feras des choix sages, \q et tu diras ce qui est vrai et sage.

sw.L: ili kushika uwezo wa kupanga, \q na midomo yako ilinde maarifa.
sw.B: ili ushike uwezo wako wa kuona mbele \q na midomo yako ilinde yale unayoyajua.
sw.R: Ndipo utakapofanya maamuzi ya hekima, \q nawe utasema yaliyo kweli na ya hekima.

decisions.choice: discretion: foresight, thinking ahead
decisions.reason: The word (mezimmah, here plural) is the one in 1:4 and 2:11. The son will need it against the smooth lips of verse 3.

decisions.choice: your lips: what you say
decisions.reason: His lips are set against hers (verse 3): his words keep knowledge, hers drip honey.

source.text: כִּ֤י נֹ֣פֶת תִּ֭טֹּפְנָה שִׂפְתֵ֣י זָרָ֑ה וְחָלָ֖ק מִשֶּׁ֣מֶן חִכָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For honey drip [the] lips of a strange [woman], and smoother than oil [is] her palate,

en.L: For the lips of a strange [woman] drip honey, \q and her palate [is] smoother than oil,
en.B: For honey drips from the lips of the woman who is not yours, \q and her talk is smoother than olive oil,
en.R: A woman who belongs to another man may say sweet things. \q Her words may seem smooth and pleasant.

fr.L: Car les lèvres de l’étrangère distillent le miel, \q et son palais [est] plus doux que l’huile,
fr.B: Car le miel coule des lèvres de la femme étrangère, qui n’est pas pour toi, \q et sa parole est plus douce que l’huile d’olive,
fr.R: La femme d’un autre peut dire des choses très douces. \q Ses paroles peuvent paraître agréables et caressantes.

sw.L: Kwa maana midomo ya [mwanamke] mgeni hudondosha asali, \q na kinywa chake [ni] laini kuliko mafuta,
sw.B: Kwa maana asali hudondoka kutoka midomoni mwa mwanamke mgeni, asiye halali yako, \q na maneno yake ni laini kuliko mafuta ya zeituni,
sw.R: Mke wa mtu mwingine anaweza kusema maneno matamu. \q Maneno yake yanaweza kuonekana laini na ya kupendeza.

decisions.choice: a strange woman: a woman who is not his to have
decisions.reason: The word (zarah) is the one in 2:16. Verses 15–20 set her against the son's own wife.

decisions.choice: honey ... smoother than oil: sweet, flattering talk
decisions.reason: Her palate (hek) stands for her speech (8:7), as in 2:16 and 7:21. The lips may also suggest her kisses (Song of Songs 4:11).

decisions.choice: the woman who is not yours
decisions.reason: As in 2:16, Balanced says what makes her "strange": she is not his to have.

source.text: וְֽ֭אַחֲרִיתָהּ מָרָ֣ה כַֽלַּעֲנָ֑ה חַ֝דָּ֗ה כְּחֶ֣רֶב פִּיּֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: but her end [is] bitter like wormwood, sharp like a sword of mouths.

en.L: but her end [is] bitter as wormwood, \q sharp as a two-edged sword.
en.B: but what she leaves you with is bitter as wormwood, \q and it cuts like a two-edged sword.
en.R: But in the end, she brings bitter pain. \q She cuts like a sharp sword.

fr.L: mais sa fin [est] amère comme l’absinthe, \q tranchante comme une épée à deux tranchants.
fr.B: mais ce qu’elle te laisse est amer comme l’absinthe, \q et cela coupe comme une épée à double tranchant.
fr.R: Mais à la fin, elle apporte une douleur amère. \q Elle blesse comme une épée bien aiguisée.

sw.L: lakini mwisho wake [ni] mchungu kama pakanga, \q mkali kama upanga wenye makali kuwili.
sw.B: lakini anachokuachia ni uchungu kama wa pakanga, \q nacho hukata kama upanga wenye makali kuwili.
sw.R: Lakini mwishowe huleta maumivu machungu. \q Hukata kama upanga mkali.

decisions.choice: wormwood: a bitter plant
decisions.reason: Wormwood (laanah) is a plant with a very bitter taste, used as a picture of bitter suffering (Lamentations 3:15; Amos 5:7).

decisions.choice: a sword of mouths: a two-edged sword
decisions.reason: A sword's edges are called its "mouths" because they "eat" (Judges 3:16).

decisions.choice: her end: what she leads to in the end
decisions.reason: "Her end" is the outcome of going with her, set against the sweetness at the start (verse 3; 14:12).

decisions.choice: "pakanga" for wormwood
decisions.reason: "Pakanga" is a bitter plant used in the Swahili Bible tradition for wormwood; Readable drops the plant and keeps the bitterness, as the English Readable does.

source.text: רַ֭גְלֶיהָ יֹרְד֣וֹת מָ֑וֶת שְׁ֝א֗וֹל צְעָדֶ֥יהָ יִתְמֹֽכוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Her feet [are] going down [to] death; [to] Sheol her steps take hold.

en.L: Her feet go down [to] death; \q her steps take hold [of] Sheol.
en.B: Her feet go down toward death; \q her steps make straight for Sheol.
en.R: The road she walks leads down to death and the grave.

fr.L: Ses pieds descendent [vers] la mort ; \q ses pas s’attachent au Shéol.
fr.B: Ses pieds descendent vers la mort ; \q ses pas mènent tout droit au séjour des morts.
fr.R: Le chemin qu’elle suit descend vers la mort et le séjour des morts.

sw.L: Miguu yake hushuka [hadi] mautini; \q hatua zake hushika [njia ya] Kuzimu.
sw.B: Miguu yake hushuka kuelekea mautini; \q hatua zake huelekea moja kwa moja Kuzimu.
sw.R: Njia anayoiendea inashuka hadi mautini na Kuzimu.

decisions.choice: her steps take hold of Sheol: they lead straight there
decisions.reason: Her steps "grasp" Sheol, the place of the dead (1:12): they go nowhere else (2:18; 7:27).

decisions.choice: Sheol
decisions.reason: As in 1:12, Literal and Balanced keep the name; Readable says "the grave".

source.text: אֹ֣רַח חַ֭יִּים פֶּן־תְּפַלֵּ֑ס נָע֥וּ מַ֝עְגְּלֹתֶ֗יהָ לֹ֣א תֵדָֽע׃פ

records.literal_gloss: [The] path of life lest she weigh, her tracks wander; she does not know.

en.L: She does not weigh [the] path of life; \q her tracks wander, [and] she does not know [it].
en.B: She does not consider the road to life; \q her ways drift, and she is unaware of it.
en.R: She does not care about living the right way. \q She wanders without knowing where she is going.

fr.L: Elle ne pèse pas le sentier de la vie ; \q ses pistes errent, [et] elle ne [le] sait pas.
fr.B: Elle ne se soucie pas du chemin de la vie ; \q ses pas s’égarent, et elle ne s’en rend pas compte.
fr.R: Elle ne cherche pas à vivre comme il faut. \q Elle erre sans savoir où elle va.

sw.L: Hapimi mapito ya uzima; \q njia zake hutangatanga, [naye] hajui.
sw.B: Hafikirii njia iendayo uzimani; \q mapito yake hupotea huku na huko, wala yeye hajui.
sw.R: Hajali kuishi kwa njia iliyo sawa. \q Hutangatanga bila kujua anakokwenda.

decisions.choice: she does not weigh the path of life
alternatives: so that you do not weigh the path of life
lest she find the path of life
decisions.reason: The line is hard. The verbs can be read as "she" or "you", and the first word (pen) means "lest". Most likely it says that she never stops to think where her road leads, so it wanders. Others read it as a warning to the son: she keeps you from thinking about the path of life.

decisions.choice: weigh: think out, make level
decisions.reason: The verb (pilles) of 4:26, where the son is told to make his own path level.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ־לִ֑י וְאַל־תָּ֝ס֗וּרוּ מֵאִמְרֵי־פִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, sons, listen to me, and do not turn aside from [the] sayings of my mouth.

en.L: And now, sons, listen to me, \q and do not turn aside from [the] sayings of my mouth.
en.B: So now, sons, hear me out, \q and do not stray from the words I speak.
en.R: So, sons, listen to me. \q Keep on doing what I tell you.

fr.L: Et maintenant, fils, écoutez-moi, \q et ne vous détournez pas des paroles de ma bouche.
fr.B: Maintenant donc, mes fils, écoutez-moi \q et ne vous écartez pas des paroles que je prononce.
fr.R: Alors, mes fils, écoutez-moi. \q Continuez à faire ce que je vous dis.

sw.L: Basi sasa, enyi wana, nisikilizeni, \q wala msigeuke kuacha maneno ya kinywa changu.
sw.B: Basi sasa, wana, nisikilizeni, \q wala msipotoke mkaacha maneno ninayosema.
sw.R: Basi, wana, nisikilizeni. \q Endeleeni kufanya yale ninayowaambia.

decisions.choice: sons: the plural address of 4:1
decisions.reason: The father turns to his sons in the plural, then back to the singular "you" in verse 8.

source.text: הַרְחֵ֣ק מֵעָלֶ֣יהָ דַרְכֶּ֑ךָ וְאַל־תִּ֝קְרַ֗ב אֶל־פֶּ֥תַח בֵּיתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Make far from her your way, and do not draw near to [the] door of her house,

en.L: Keep your way far from her, \q and do not draw near to [the] door of her house,
en.B: Keep well away from her, \q and do not even come near her front door,
en.R: Stay far away from her. \q Do not even go near the door of her house.

fr.L: Éloigne d’elle ton chemin, \q et ne t’approche pas de la porte de sa maison,
fr.B: Tiens-toi bien loin d’elle, \q et ne t’approche même pas de sa porte,
fr.R: Reste loin d’elle. \q Ne va même pas près de la porte de sa maison.

sw.L: Iweke njia yako mbali naye, \q wala usikaribie mlango wa nyumba yake,
sw.B: Kaa mbali naye kabisa, \q wala usikaribie hata mlango wa nyumba yake,
sw.R: Kaa mbali naye kabisa. \q Usikaribie hata mlango wa nyumba yake.

decisions.choice: the door of her house: where temptation is met
decisions.reason: Chapter 7 tells of a young man who walks by her corner and is drawn in at her door (7:8, 27). The father's advice is distance.

source.text: פֶּן־תִּתֵּ֣ן לַאֲחֵרִ֣ים הוֹדֶ֑ךָ וּ֝שְׁנֹתֶ֗יךָ לְאַכְזָרִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: lest you give to others your splendor, and your years to a cruel [one],

en.L: lest you give your splendor to others, \q and your years to a cruel [one],
en.B: or you will hand over your strength to others \q and your years to someone without mercy,
en.R: If you do, other people will take your strength, \q and a cruel person will take the best years of your life.

fr.L: de peur que tu ne donnes à d’autres ta vigueur, \q et tes années à un [homme] cruel,
fr.B: sinon tu livreras ta force à d’autres \q et tes années à quelqu’un qui sera sans pitié,
fr.R: Sinon, d’autres prendront ta force, \q et une personne cruelle prendra les meilleures années de ta vie.

sw.L: usije ukawapa wengine fahari yako, \q na miaka yako kwa [mtu] mkatili,
sw.B: la sivyo utawakabidhi wengine nguvu zako \q na miaka yako kwa mtu asiye na huruma,
sw.R: Ukifanya hivyo, watu wengine watachukua nguvu zako, \q na mtu mkatili atachukua miaka bora ya maisha yako.

decisions.choice: splendor: vigor, the best of a man's strength
decisions.reason: The word (hod) means majesty or splendor (Psalm 45:4). Here it is the vigor and dignity of a man's life, spent on others.

decisions.choice: a cruel one: someone who will show no mercy
decisions.reason: The verse does not say who it is. It may be the woman's husband, who will take revenge (6:34–35), or anyone who takes advantage of a man caught in adultery.

source.text: פֶּֽן־יִשְׂבְּע֣וּ זָרִ֣ים כֹּחֶ֑ךָ וַ֝עֲצָבֶ֗יךָ בְּבֵ֣ית נָכְרִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: lest strangers be sated [with] your strength, and your toils [be] in [the] house of a foreigner,

en.L: lest strangers be filled [with] your strength, \q and your toils [go] to [the] house of a foreigner,
en.B: and strangers will feed on your wealth, \q and what you worked hard for will end up in an outsider's house,
en.R: Strangers will enjoy your money, \q and what you worked for will belong to someone else's family.

fr.L: de peur que des étrangers ne se rassasient de ta force, \q et que tes peines [n’aillent] à la maison d’un inconnu,
fr.B: des étrangers se nourriront de tes biens, \q et ce que tu as gagné à la sueur de ton front finira dans la maison d’un inconnu,
fr.R: Des étrangers profiteront de ton argent, \q et ce que tu as gagné en travaillant appartiendra à une autre famille.

sw.L: wageni wasije wakashiba nguvu zako, \q na taabu zako [zikaenda] katika nyumba ya mgeni,
sw.B: na wageni watajilisha kwa mali yako, \q na ulichokitaabikia kitaishia katika nyumba ya mtu wa nje,
sw.R: Wageni watafurahia fedha yako, \q na ulichokifanyia kazi kitakuwa mali ya jamaa ya mtu mwingine.

decisions.choice: your strength: your wealth, the product of your strength
decisions.reason: The word (koah) is strength, and also what strength earns (Job 6:22).

decisions.choice: strangers ... a foreigner: outsiders
decisions.reason: The same two words used of the woman in 2:16 and 5:20. Her world takes what was his.

source.text: וְנָהַמְתָּ֥ בְאַחֲרִיתֶ֑ךָ בִּכְל֥וֹת בְּ֝שָׂרְךָ֗ וּשְׁאֵרֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: and you will groan at your end, when your flesh and your body are consumed,

en.L: and you will groan at your end, \q when your flesh and your body are consumed,
en.B: and when it is all over you will groan, \q your body wasted and your flesh used up,
en.R: At the end, your body will be worn out, \q and you will cry in pain.

fr.L: et tu gémiras à ta fin, \q quand ta chair et ton corps seront consumés,
fr.B: et quand tout sera fini, tu gémiras, \q le corps usé et la chair épuisée,
fr.R: À la fin, ton corps sera usé, \q et tu pleureras de douleur.

sw.L: nawe utaugua mwishoni mwako, \q nyama yako na mwili wako vitakapoliwa,
sw.B: na yote yatakapokwisha utalia kwa uchungu, \q mwili wako umedhoofika na nyama yako imekwisha,
sw.R: Mwishoni mwili wako utachakaa, \q nawe utalia kwa maumivu.

decisions.choice: groan: moan in distress
decisions.reason: The verb (naham) is used of a lion's growl (19:12) and of the moaning of the suffering (Ezekiel 24:23).

decisions.choice: your flesh and your body are consumed: worn out
decisions.reason: The verse does not say how: by disease, by poverty, or simply by a life spent badly. It is the bitter end of verse 4.

source.text: וְֽאָמַרְתָּ֗ אֵ֭יךְ שָׂנֵ֣אתִי מוּסָ֑ר וְ֝תוֹכַ֗חַת נָאַ֥ץ לִבִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: and you will say, How I hated discipline, and rebuke my heart despised,

en.L: and you will say, "How I hated discipline, \q and my heart despised rebuke!
en.B: and you will say, "How I hated being corrected! \q How my heart despised every warning!
en.R: Then you will say, "Why did I hate it when people corrected me? \q Why did I refuse to listen to warnings?

fr.L: et tu diras : « Comme j’ai haï la discipline, \q et mon cœur a méprisé la réprimande !
fr.B: et tu diras : « Comme j’ai détesté qu’on me corrige ! \q Comme mon cœur a méprisé tous les avertissements !
fr.R: Alors tu diras : « Pourquoi est-ce que je détestais qu’on me corrige ? \q Pourquoi est-ce que j’ai refusé d’écouter les avertissements ?

sw.L: nawe utasema, "Jinsi nilivyochukia nidhamu, \q na moyo wangu ukadharau karipio!
sw.B: nawe utasema, "Jinsi nilivyochukia kuonywa! \q Jinsi moyo wangu ulivyodharau kila onyo!
sw.R: Ndipo utasema, "Kwa nini nilichukia watu waliponionya? \q Kwa nini nilikataa kusikiliza maonyo?

decisions.choice: you will say: the son's regret, running to the end of verse 14
decisions.reason: The father puts into the son's mouth the words he would say too late (1:24–31).

source.text: וְֽלֹא־שָׁ֭מַעְתִּי בְּק֣וֹל מוֹרָ֑י וְ֝לִֽמְלַמְּדַ֗י לֹא־הִטִּ֥יתִי אָזְנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: and I did not listen to [the] voice of my teachers, and to my instructors I did not incline my ear.

en.L: I did not listen to [the] voice of my teachers, \q and to my instructors I did not incline my ear.
en.B: I paid no attention to what my teachers said; \q I would not lend an ear to those who taught me.
en.R: I did not listen to my teachers. \q I did not pay attention to the people who taught me.

fr.L: Je n’ai pas écouté la voix de mes maîtres, \q et à ceux qui m’instruisaient je n’ai pas incliné mon oreille.
fr.B: Je n’ai pas prêté attention à ce que disaient mes maîtres ; \q je n’ai pas voulu écouter ceux qui m’enseignaient.
fr.R: Je n’ai pas écouté mes maîtres. \q Je n’ai pas fait attention aux gens qui m’enseignaient.

sw.L: Sikuisikiliza sauti ya walimu wangu, \q wala sikutega sikio langu kwa wakufunzi wangu.
sw.B: Sikujali walimu wangu waliyosema; \q sikuwategea sikio wale walionifundisha.
sw.R: Sikuwasikiliza walimu wangu. \q Sikuwajali watu walionifundisha.

decisions.choice: teachers ... instructors: the father and others who taught
decisions.reason: The first word (moreh) is from the root of torah, teaching (4:2, 11). The father counts himself among them.

source.text: כִּ֭מְעַט הָיִ֣יתִי בְכָל־רָ֑ע בְּת֖וֹךְ קָהָ֣ל וְעֵדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Almost I was in every evil in [the] midst of [the] assembly and congregation.

en.L: Almost I was in every evil, \q in [the] midst of [the] assembly and congregation."
en.B: I came close to complete ruin, \q there in front of the whole assembled community."
en.R: Now I am almost completely ruined, \q and everyone knows it."

fr.L: Peu s’en est fallu que je sois dans tout le mal, \q au milieu de l’assemblée et de la communauté. »
fr.B: J’ai bien failli tomber dans la ruine complète, \q là, devant toute la communauté rassemblée. »
fr.R: Maintenant, je suis presque complètement ruiné, \q et tout le monde le sait. »

sw.L: Karibu nilikuwa katika kila ubaya, \q katikati ya kusanyiko na jumuiya."
sw.B: Nilikaribia kuangamia kabisa, \q hapo mbele ya jumuiya yote iliyokusanyika."
sw.R: Sasa karibu nimeangamia kabisa, \q na kila mtu anajua."

decisions.choice: almost in every evil: close to complete ruin
alternatives: in a moment I was in great trouble
decisions.reason: The phrase (kimat) can mean "almost" or "in a moment". Either way he has come to ruin.

decisions.choice: the assembly and congregation: the community, gathered for judgment
decisions.reason: The two words name the people of Israel gathered together. Adultery could be judged in public (Deuteronomy 22:22; 6:33), so his ruin is public shame, and may be a legal penalty.

decisions.choice: "l'assemblée" (qahal) and "la communauté" (ʿedah)
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch terms set them for the whole Old Testament in French: "l'assemblée" for qahal, "la communauté" for ʿedah.

source.text: שְׁתֵה־מַ֥יִם מִבּוֹרֶ֑ךָ וְ֝נֹזְלִ֗ים מִתּ֥וֹךְ בְּאֵרֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Drink water from your cistern, and flowing [water] from [the] midst of your well.

en.L: Drink water from your [own] cistern, \q and flowing [water] from [the] midst of your [own] well.
en.B: Draw your water from your own cistern, \q the fresh streams from inside your own well.
en.R: Be faithful to your own wife and enjoy her love, \q like a man who drinks water from his own well.

fr.L: Bois l’eau de ta [propre] citerne, \q et ce qui coule du milieu de ton [propre] puits.
fr.B: Puise l’eau dans ta propre citerne, \q l’eau vive au fond de ton propre puits.
fr.R: Sois fidèle à ta femme et profite de son amour, \q comme un homme qui boit l’eau de son propre puits.

sw.L: Kunywa maji kutoka kisima chako [mwenyewe], \q na [maji] yanayotiririka kutoka ndani ya chemchemi yako [mwenyewe].
sw.B: Teka maji kutoka katika birika lako mwenyewe, \q mito safi kutoka ndani ya kisima chako mwenyewe.
sw.R: Uwe mwaminifu kwa mke wako mwenyewe na ufurahie upendo wake, \q kama mtu anayekunywa maji ya kisima chake mwenyewe.

decisions.choice: drink water from your own cistern: find love with your own wife
decisions.reason: In a dry land, a cistern or well of one's own was precious. The Song of Songs uses the same pictures of a bride (Song of Songs 4:12, 15). Verse 18 names her: "the wife of your youth".

decisions.choice: Be faithful to your own wife
alternatives: Drink water from your own cistern
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1) and keeps it as a comparison.

source.text: יָפ֣וּצוּ מַעְיְנֹתֶ֣יךָ ח֑וּצָה בָּ֝רְחֹב֗וֹת פַּלְגֵי־מָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: Should your springs overflow outside, in the squares streams of water?

en.L: Should your springs overflow outside, \q streams of water in the squares?
en.B: Why let your springs run out into the street, \q and your streams flow through the town squares?
en.R: Why waste your love on other women, \q like water spilling into the street?

fr.L: Tes sources se répandraient-elles au-dehors, \q des ruisseaux d’eau sur les places ?
fr.B: Pourquoi laisser tes sources couler dans la rue \q et tes ruisseaux sur les places publiques ?
fr.R: Pourquoi gaspiller ton amour avec d’autres femmes, \q comme de l’eau qu’on renverse dans la rue ?

sw.L: Je, chemchemi zako zifurike nje, \q vijito vya maji katika viwanja?
sw.B: Kwa nini chemchemi zako zimwagike barabarani, \q na vijito vyako vitiririke katika viwanja vya mji?
sw.R: Kwa nini upoteze upendo wako kwa wanawake wengine, \q kama maji yanayomwagika barabarani?

decisions.choice: should your springs overflow outside? a question expecting "no"
alternatives: Let your springs flow outside (a statement)
decisions.reason: Hebrew does not always mark a question. Read as a question, the verse warns against wasting the son's love on other women, and verse 17 follows: "let them be yours alone". Some read it as a promise of children; others as the wife's love flowing to others if he is unfaithful.

source.text: יִֽהְיוּ־לְךָ֥ לְבַדֶּ֑ךָ וְאֵ֖ין לְזָרִ֣ים אִתָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Let them be to you alone, and not to strangers with you.

en.L: Let them be for you alone, \q and not for strangers with you.
en.B: Keep them for yourself alone, \q with no strangers drinking beside you.
en.R: Your love should be for you and your wife alone, \q not for anyone else.

fr.L: Qu’elles soient pour toi seul, \q et non pour des étrangers avec toi.
fr.B: Garde-les pour toi seul, \q sans étrangers qui boivent à côté de toi.
fr.R: Ton amour doit être pour toi et ta femme seulement, \q pas pour quelqu’un d’autre.

sw.L: Yawe yako peke yako, \q wala si ya wageni pamoja nawe.
sw.B: Yaweke kwa ajili yako peke yako, \q bila wageni kunywa pamoja nawe.
sw.R: Upendo wako uwe kwa ajili yako na mke wako peke yenu, \q si kwa mtu mwingine yeyote.

decisions.choice: strangers: outsiders
decisions.reason: The word (zarim) is the one used of the strange woman (5:3, 20) and of those who take his strength (5:10).

source.text: יְהִֽי־מְקוֹרְךָ֥ בָר֑וּךְ וּ֝שְׂמַ֗ח מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת נְעוּרֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: May your fountain be blessed, and rejoice in [the] wife of your youth,

en.L: Let your fountain be blessed, \q and rejoice in [the] wife of your youth,
en.B: May your spring be blessed; \q find your joy in the woman you married when you were young,
en.R: May God bless your marriage. \q Be happy with the woman you married when you were young.

fr.L: Que ta fontaine soit bénie, \q et réjouis-toi de la femme de ta jeunesse,
fr.B: Que ta source soit bénie ; \q trouve ta joie dans la femme que tu as épousée quand tu étais jeune,
fr.R: Que Dieu bénisse ton mariage. \q Sois heureux avec la femme que tu as épousée quand tu étais jeune.

sw.L: Chemchemi yako na ibarikiwe, \q nawe ufurahi na mke wa ujana wako,
sw.B: Chemchemi yako na ibarikiwe; \q ufurahi na mwanamke uliyemwoa ulipokuwa kijana,
sw.R: Mungu aibariki ndoa yako. \q Ufurahi na mwanamke uliyemwoa ulipokuwa kijana.

decisions.choice: blessed: blessed by God
decisions.reason: This word (baruk) is used of what God blesses, unlike "how blessed" (ashre) in 3:13. The fountain is his wife, and the blessing may include children.

decisions.choice: the wife of your youth: the wife he married when young
decisions.reason: The phrase looks back to the start of the marriage (2:17; Malachi 2:14–15).

decisions.choice: May God bless your marriage
decisions.reason: Readable names God, the one who blesses (m1), and says what the fountain stands for.

source.text: אַיֶּ֥לֶת אֲהָבִ֗ים וְֽיַעֲלַ֫ת־חֵ֥ן דַּ֭דֶּיהָ יְרַוֻּ֣ךָ בְכָל־עֵ֑ת בְּ֝אַהֲבָתָ֗הּ תִּשְׁגֶּ֥ה תָמִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: a doe of love and a mountain goat of grace; her breasts, may they satisfy you at every time; by her love may you be intoxicated continually.

en.L: a doe of love and a mountain goat of grace; \q let her breasts satisfy you at all times; \q by her love be intoxicated continually.
en.B: a lovely doe, a graceful mountain goat. \q Let her breasts content you at every season, \q and let her love carry you away always.
en.R: She is beautiful and lovely, like a young deer. \q Let her body always satisfy you. \q Let her love fill you with joy.

fr.L: biche d’amour et chèvre des montagnes pleine de grâce ; \q que ses seins te comblent en tout temps ; \q de son amour sois enivré sans cesse.
fr.B: une biche charmante, une gracieuse chèvre des montagnes. \q Que ses seins te comblent en toute saison, \q et que son amour te transporte toujours.
fr.R: Elle est belle et charmante, comme une jeune biche. \q Que son corps te comble toujours. \q Que son amour te remplisse de joie.

sw.L: ayala wa upendo na mbuzi-mwitu wa neema; \q matiti yake yakutoshelezee kila wakati; \q kwa upendo wake ulewe daima.
sw.B: ayala mzuri, mbuzi-mwitu wa kupendeza. \q Matiti yake yakutosheleze kila wakati, \q na upendo wake ukuchukue siku zote.
sw.R: Yeye ni mzuri na wa kupendeza, kama paa mchanga. \q Mwili wake ukutosheleze siku zote. \q Upendo wake ukujaze furaha.

decisions.choice: a doe ... a mountain goat: pictures of a woman's beauty
decisions.reason: The doe and the wild goat were known for their grace and beauty. The Song of Songs uses such animals in its love poetry (Song of Songs 2:9; 4:5).

decisions.choice: be intoxicated: be carried away, as if drunk
decisions.reason: The verb (shagah) means to reel or stagger, and so to go astray. The father uses it three times: be carried away by your wife's love (verse 19), not by another woman (verse 20), or you will be carried away to death by your folly (verse 23).

decisions.choice: carry you away
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the same English verb in verses 19, 20 and 23, so the reader can see the wordplay (m2).

decisions.choice: "ulewe" (be drunk) at Literal, so that the same verb returns in verses 20 and 23
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one verb for being drunk with a wife's love, with another woman, and for the fool's staggering; Literal keeps the repeated picture with "kulewa" and "kuyumbayumba", Balanced says "ukuchukue" as the English says "carry you away".

source.text: וְלָ֤מָּה תִשְׁגֶּ֣ה בְנִ֣י בְזָרָ֑ה וּ֝תְחַבֵּ֗ק חֵ֣ק נָכְרִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And why should you be intoxicated, my son, with a strange [woman], and embrace [the] bosom of a foreign [woman]?

en.L: Why should you be intoxicated, my son, with a strange [woman], \q and embrace [the] bosom of a foreign [woman]?
en.B: Why, my son, let yourself be carried away by a woman who is not yours, \q or take an outsider in your arms?
en.R: My son, why let another man's wife excite you? \q Why hold her in your arms?

fr.L: Pourquoi serais-tu enivré, mon fils, par une étrangère, \q et embrasserais-tu le sein d’une inconnue ?
fr.B: Pourquoi, mon fils, te laisser transporter par une femme qui n’est pas pour toi, \q ou prendre une inconnue dans tes bras ?
fr.R: Mon fils, pourquoi te laisser exciter par la femme d’un autre ? \q Pourquoi la prendre dans tes bras ?

sw.L: Kwa nini, mwanangu, ulewe na [mwanamke] mgeni, \q na kukumbatia kifua cha [mwanamke] wa kigeni?
sw.B: Mwanangu, kwa nini ujiache uchukuliwe na mwanamke asiye halali yako, \q au umkumbatie mgeni?
sw.R: Mwanangu, kwa nini ukubali mke wa mtu mwingine akuvutie? \q Kwa nini umkumbatie?

decisions.choice: a strange woman ... a foreign woman: as in 2:16
decisions.reason: The same pair of words as in 2:16; the father has come back to where the chapter began (verse 3).

source.text: כִּ֤י נֹ֨כַח׀עֵינֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה דַּרְכֵי־אִ֑ישׁ וְֽכָל־מַעְגְּלֹתָ֥יו מְפַלֵּֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: For before [the] eyes of YHWH [are the] ways of a man, and all his tracks he weighs.

en.L: For before [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [are the] ways of {{gender:a person|a man}}, \q and all {{gender:their|his}} tracks {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} weighs.
en.B: For everything a person does is in plain view of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} weighs every path they take.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sees everything people do. \q He watches every step they take.

fr.L: Car devant les yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} [sont] les chemins de {{gender:la personne|l’homme}}, \q et toutes ses pistes, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} [les] pèse.
fr.B: Car tout ce que fait chacun est sous les yeux {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pèse chaque sentier qu’il prend.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} voit tout ce que font les gens. \q Il observe chacun de leurs pas.

sw.L: Kwa maana mbele ya macho ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [ziko] njia za mtu, \q na mapito yake yote huyapima.
sw.B: Kwa maana kila anachofanya mtu kiko wazi mbele ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q naye huipima kila njia anayoifuata.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} huona kila kitu wanachofanya watu. \q Huangalia kila hatua wanayopiga.

decisions.choice: weighs: examines, or makes level
decisions.reason: The verb (pilles) of 4:26 and 5:6. The LORD looks over every road a person takes, so nothing done in secret is hidden from him (15:3; Job 31:4).

decisions.choice: a man: anyone
decisions.reason: The word (ish) here means any person, though the warning is to the son.

source.text: עַֽווֹנוֹתָ֗יויִלְכְּדֻנ֥וֹ אֶת־הָרָשָׁ֑ע וּבְחַבְלֵ֥י חַ֝טָּאת֗וֹ יִתָּמֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: His iniquities will capture him, the wicked, and in [the] cords of his sin he will be held.

en.L: {{gender:Their|His}} iniquities will capture the wicked, \q and in [the] cords of {{gender:their|his}} sin {{gender:they|he}} will be held.
en.B: Their own wrongdoing will catch the wicked, \q and the ropes of their sin will tie them up.
en.R: Evil people get trapped by the bad things they do. \q Their sins are like ropes that tie them up.

fr.L: Ses fautes captureront le méchant, \q et dans les cordes de son péché il sera retenu.
fr.B: Le méchant sera pris par ses propres fautes, \q et les cordes de son péché le ligoteront.
fr.R: Les méchants se font prendre par le mal qu’ils font. \q Leurs péchés sont comme des cordes qui les attachent.

sw.L: Maovu yake yatamnasa mwovu, \q naye atashikwa kwa kamba za dhambi yake.
sw.B: Uovu wao wenyewe utawanasa waovu, \q na kamba za dhambi yao zitawafunga.
sw.R: Watu waovu hunaswa na mabaya wanayoyatenda. \q Dhambi zao ni kama kamba zinazowafunga.

decisions.choice: capture ... cords: sin is a trap the sinner sets for himself
decisions.reason: The picture is of a hunter's snare. The wicked need no one else to catch them (1:18; Psalm 7:16–17).

source.text: ה֗וּא יָ֭מוּת בְּאֵ֣ין מוּסָ֑ר וּבְרֹ֖ב אִוַּלְתּ֣וֹ יִשְׁגֶּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: He will die for lack of discipline, and in [the] greatness of his folly he will go astray.

en.L: {{gender:They|He}} will die for lack of discipline, \q and in [the] greatness of {{gender:their|his}} folly {{gender:they|he}} will stagger.
en.B: Such people die for lack of discipline, \q carried away by their great folly.
en.R: They will die because they would not accept correction. \q Their great foolishness will lead them away.

fr.L: Il mourra faute de discipline, \q et dans la grandeur de sa folie il chancellera.
fr.B: Il mourra faute de discipline, \q emporté par sa grande folie.
fr.R: Ils mourront parce qu’ils n’ont pas voulu accepter la correction. \q Leur grande folie les entraînera au loin.

sw.L: Atakufa kwa kukosa nidhamu, \q na katika wingi wa upumbavu wake atayumbayumba.
sw.B: Watu kama hao hufa kwa kukosa nidhamu, \q wakichukuliwa na upumbavu wao mkuu.
sw.R: Watakufa kwa sababu walikataa kuonywa. \q Upumbavu wao mkubwa utawapeleka mbali.

decisions.choice: stagger: be carried away, go astray
decisions.reason: The verb (shagah) of verses 19–20. The man who was carried away by a strange woman is now carried away to death.

decisions.choice: folly: the stubbornness of the fool
decisions.reason: The word (iwwelet) belongs to the fool of 1:7, who despises discipline.
